 “(California Government Code Section 54954.3).
 (a) Every agenda for regular meetings shall provide an opportunity for members of the
 public to directly address the legislative body on any item of interest to the public, before
 or during the legislative body’s consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter
 jurisdiction of the legislative body, provided that no action shall be taken on any item not
 appearing on the agenda unless the action is otherwise authorized by subdivision (b) of
 Section 54954.2 [section omitted].

City Council  Wednesday, August 7, 2024
  (b) (1) The legislative body of a local agency may adopt reasonable regulations to ensure
 that the intent of the subdivision (a) is carried out, including, but not limited to, regulations
 limiting the total amount of time allocated for public testimony on particular issues and for
 each individual speaker.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), when the legislative body of a local agency limits
 time for public comment, the legislative body of a local agency shall provide at least twice
 the allotted time to a member of the public who utilizes a translator to ensure that non-
 English speakers receive the same opportunity to directly address the legislative body of
 a local agency.”

 In furtherance of Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act, the public is allotted to speak a total
 of two (2) minutes on the entirety of the Consent Calendar, Appointment(s), New
 Business and Closed Session, with two (2) minutes on each Public Hearing, and, if
 desired, an additional two (2) minutes on items not on the agenda that are within the
 subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council. As specified in the Brown Act, a speaker
 utilizing a translator will receive twice the amount of time specified.

SUBJECT:  RECEIVE AND FILE THE MONTHLY AND QUARTERLY
  INVESTMENT ACTIVITY REPORTS FOR JUNE 2024

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the monthly and quarterly
investment activity reports for the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency for June
2024.

BACKGROUND

Pursuant to Section 16 of the City and Successor Agency Investment Policy, the City
Treasurer shall prepare and present monthly and quarterly reports on investments to
the City Manager/Executive Director and the City Council/Directors. The reports shall
detail the type of investment, issuer’s name, purchase date, maturity date, amount of
deposit, and interest rate. This information shall be provided for all City and Successor
Agency pooled investments and for Certificates of Participation, Revenue Bonds, Tax
Allocation Bonds, Assessment Districts, and Community Facilities District accounts
managed by outside Fiscal Agents.

The monthly investment reports provide a synopsis of the City and Successor Agency's
investment activity. They provide information on assets, allocations, average maturities,
yields, and book valuations. The interest rates presented are the most current rates
available as of the date of this report.

The market values presented for pooled City and Successor Agency investments are
based on closing prices for the related investment as of the date of this report. This
information was obtained from the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg Financial Markets,
Capital Market Finances, or other reliable sources of market prices.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Monthly and Quarterly Investment Reports
August 7, 2024
Page 2

DISCUSSION

Compliance with Investment Policy

For June, the City’s invested portfolio totaled $345,612,779, an increase of $6,455,905
from the previous month and an increase of $22,311,569 compared to last year. The
monthly increase resulted from a new investment purchase made during the month and
from transfer of funds to California Asset Management Program (CAMP).

The par value of Successor Agency’s portfolio as of June was $12,604,544. The balance
increased by $3,412,021 from last month due to funds received from Los Angeles
County for property taxes during the month.

All investments meet criteria appropriate to Section 8 of the Investment Policy. The
portfolios are based on a combination of various investments, including CDs, Corporate
Notes, US Treasury Securities, and Government Agency Paper, each adhering to
portfolio percentage limitations.

The Finance Division is the custodian for the City and Successor Agency’s investment
portfolio and follows the three main principles of both entities’ investment policies: 1)
Investment in financial instruments that mitigate the risk of monetary losses stemming
from market fluctuations; 2) Establish and maintain a portfolio that has sufficient liquidity
to allow the City and Successor Agency to meet all anticipated cash requirements; and,
3) Seek out investment instruments that provide a competitive market rate of return.

Liquidity

One core approach the Finance Division focuses on is providing liquidity to meet the
City and Successor Agency’s operational requirements. Thus, the Finance Division
invests in two pooled funds, LAIF and CAMP. These are intended for daily operational
activities and can be used during economic uncertainties for ongoing maintenance
needs. The pooled funds provide a higher liquidity ratio to ensure the City and Successor
Agency meet cash flow requirements.

The City's LAIF balance at the end of June was $122,620,640, with no changes from
the prior month.

The Successor Agency’s LAIF balance at the end of June was $8,150,476, with no
changes from the prior month.

The City’s CAMP balance at the end of June was $47,472,526, compared to
$40,788,078 in May. The increase is due to deposits into the fund, and interest earned
during the month.

Re: Monthly and Quarterly Investment Reports

The interest rates presented are the most current rates available as of the date of this
report. As of June 30, 2024, the interest rates for LAIF and CAMP investments were at
4.480 percent and 5.43 percent, respectively. By comparison, the LAIF and CAMP
interest rates at the end of May were 4.332 percent and 5.43 percent. This time last
year, LAIF and CAMP rates were at 3.167 percent and 5.24, respectively.

The chart above shows the LAIF and CAMP average monthly yields from September
2023 through June 2024. The difference between the two funds’ performance is
primarily due to their varying pool characteristics. CAMP’s portfolio composition is more
prone to market volatility, resulting in performance variations.

Diversity

The Finance Division aims to diversify the investment portfolios to avoid incurring
unreasonable and avoidable risks regarding specific security types or individual financial
institutions.

The City and Successor Agency’s investment portfolios remain strongly diversified. The
monthly and quarterly reports includes all investments held by both entities and current
book values as of June 30, 2024.

The City and Successor Agency are expected to have sufficient funds to meet its
expenditure requirements for the next six months. The Finance Division will continue to
monitor current economic conditions and the impact on interest rates.

Attached are summaries of the investments in the City and Successor Agency’s books
as of June 30, 2024.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. 8926 with Willdan Engineering (Willdan) to provide
  Innovative Solutions and Smart City Program consulting services in an amount not
  to exceed $750,000 for a term of three (3) years with an option to extend two one-
  year terms in an amount not to exceed $250,000 each additional year;

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8929
  with Willdan, including minimal and/or non-substantial changes; and,

  3. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to exercise the option to extend two
  additional one-year terms and execute the agreements, including minimal and/or
  non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

On April 15, 2024, the City initiated a competitive bidding process to procure a creative
and impartial third-party consultant to bolster the City’s Innovative Solutions and Smart
City Program. This program is designed to serve as a testing ground for pioneering
concepts, validating their practical benefits within our community.

August 7, 2024

The selected consultant will play a pivotal role in identifying and implementing Smart
City technologies and innovative solutions, guiding the City toward a seamless transition
into the future.

DISCUSSION

Following a thorough evaluation of multiple proposals, Willdan emerged as the preferred
consultant to support the City's Innovative Solutions and Smart City Program. Willdan
will oversee and manage the Program, which aims to establish a platform for testing and
validating new ideas in real-world scenarios. Their strategic approach will focus on
integrating Smart City technologies and innovative solutions to advance the City's
progress.

Key responsibilities entrusted to Willdan will include proactive engagement in marketing
and outreach efforts, facilitation of City procedures, provision of technical guidance,
meticulous oversight of project implementations, effective project management, and
rigorous evaluation of both programs and projects.

FISCAL IMPACT

$750,000; Program funds are allocated under Professional Services Account No.
10118001-721960. The cost of the consulting agreement is not to exceed $250,000 per
year. Subsequent years will be allocated through the budget process.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal III: Invest in infrastructure to improve community livability.

  A. Seek innovative, cost effective, customer focused methods of service delivery.
  B. Implement and administer environmentally sustainable programs.

SUBJECT:  APPROVE AGREEMENT WITH JAD HOYOS, INC., DBA FEATHERS
  CUSTOM SIGNS TO PROVIDE ANTI-GRAFFITI VINYL WRAP
  SERVICES FOR 160 CITY-OWNED UTILITY CABINETS ALONG
  ROADWAYS IN THE AMOUNT OF $150,000 FOR A TERM OF ONE
  YEAR WITH THE OPTION TO EXTEND TWO ONE-YEAR TERMS

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8927 with JAD Hoyos, Inc., dba Feathers Custom Signs
  to provide anti-graffiti vinyl wrap services for 160 City-owned utility cabinets along
  roadways in the amount of $150,000 for a term of one year with the option to
  extend two one-year terms;

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8927
  with JAD Hoyos, Inc., dba Feathers Custom Signs, including minimal and/or non-
  substantial changes; and,

  3. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to exercise the option to extend two
  additional one-year terms and execute each agreement, including minimal and/or
  non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

The City’s graffiti abatement team responds to over 1,000 graffiti reports per year. On
March 15, 2023, the City Council approved Agreement No. A-8266 with Feathers
Custom Signs to wrap 103 traffic control utility cabinets with a graffiti-resistant laminate
that facilitates the removal of graffiti paint and markers, reducing response time if
tagged. These vinyl wraps have been well received by the community, as they enhance
public spaces with artwork that represents our region.

The City is now proposing to wrap 160 roadway utility cabinets to continue graffiti
abatement and community beautification efforts. Imagery reflecting Palmdale’s natural
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Agreement No. A-8927 with Feathers Custom Signs
August 7, 2024

landscape and habitat, featuring wildflowers, birds, and reptiles, was selected. Fifteen
images were presented to the community via a survey, resulting in the top three choices:
Joshua trees, poppy flowers, and cacti. The survey was widely promoted through an e-
newsletter, a press release, and social media boosts, resulting in nearly 300 responses
from the public.

DISCUSSION

The City released an Invitation for Bids (IFB) No. 24-001-4400 for vinyl wrap services
on April 23, 2024. Notifications were released through PlanetBids and sent to 12 service
vendors. The City received two complete bids. Upon reviewing the bid responses and
reference checks, Feathers Custom Signs was found to be the lowest responsible and
responsive bidder. Staff recommends awarding Feathers Custom Signs Agreement No.
A-8927 in the amount of $150,000.

Vinyl wrap services include the cleaning, degreasing, and pressure washing of the
surface of each item to ensure the longevity of material installation. The material used will
include anti-graffiti laminate that will be UV-protected. Feathers Custom Signs will provide
all needed materials, develop appropriate measurements per item, print all graphics, and
manage future repairs and maintenance. The wraps have an average lifespan of five to
seven years, depending on weather and outdoor conditions. The wrapping of these
remaining 160 utility cabinets supports the City’s efforts to combat graffiti.

FISCAL IMPACT

$150,000; Funds are budgeted and available in FY 2024-25 in Measure AV account
No. 15733002-737100.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Fourth Amendment to Agreement No. A-6081 with Library Systems and
  Services, LLC, for Literacy and English as a Second Language (ESL) services at
  the Palmdale City Library, increasing the agreement by $349,472 for a total not to
  exceed amount of $13,109,618 for the remainder of the term through June 2028;
  and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to approve changes, amendments,
  services, equipment, and supplies up to 10% of the contract total.

BACKGROUND

Library Systems and Services, LLC has provided Library operations and programs at
the Palmdale City Library since 2012. The current agreement, which began in 2018, is
for a 10-year term.

In 2021, the Palmdale City Library conducted a needs assessment, resulting in a five-
year strategic plan. The plan identified several key focus areas, including:

  1) Serving the Spanish speakers through programs and collections.

To achieve these goals, the Library secured a grant from the California State Library to
offer Literacy and English as a Second Language (ESL) programs. The grant funds most
program costs, including a full-time literacy services coordinator, materials, and
volunteer training.

DISCUSSION

The Library’s Literacy and ESL programming, initiated in December 2023, has
successfully engaged 48 participants who received 320 hours of individualized services
with a total attendance of over 2,500 between classes, sessions, and events. This
achievement has been made possible through the dedicated efforts of 18 volunteer
tutors. The program receives new applications weekly, reflecting its growing impact and
ongoing expansion.

contract by an additional $349,472. This amount will fund services to complete the 10-
year term through June 30, 2028.

Recreation accounts 10124001 – Library General Fund, 15824001 – American Rescue
Plan Act (ARPA), and 24224001 – Library Grant, for fiscal year 24/25. Funding for
services in fiscal years 2024-25 through 2027-28 will be evaluated and approved as part
of the annual budget adoption process.

  Library Service Delivery Agreement

A.  Statement of Work

LS&S will administer the operations of City's library facilities (collectively, "Library"), including the
accounting for, purchase of and payment for payroll services and goods and services from vendors for
budgeted supplies, other direct operating expenditures, Library Materials (as defined below) and Capital
Items (as defined below) sufficient to operate the Library in accordance with the policies and guidelines
approved by City.

LS&S shall provide, by and through its own employees or independent contractors ("LS&S Staff') any
labor LS&S deems necessary for the operation of the Library. The cost of the LS&S Staff shall be paid
by LS&S and is included in the Operating Budget (as defined below). LS&S shall have the sole and
absolute right to hire, manage, evaluate and terminate the employment of the LS&S Staff from time to
time to perform work under this Agreement. However, the City Manager will have the right to approve
the selection of the Library Director. LS&S will provide the appropriate staffing levels to keep the
Library open to the public for fifty-eight (58) hours per week. The Library will be closed on some
Holidays and other days mutually agreed upon in writing by the City and LS&S.

Hours of operation of the Library:

Monday - Thursday: 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.
Friday - Saturday: 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Sunday: I p.m. to 5 p.m.

A.  Scope of Work

  a.  General - Under the general direction of the City Manager or his designee, administer all
  aspects of the day-to-day operations of the Library, in accordance with generally
  accepted practices and principles of the public library profession. Annually review
  collections, program development ensuring that programming, services and collections
  are in line with community needs and strategic plan. Comply with all California laws and
  regulations pertaining to public library services, including, but not limited to, the
  California Library Services Act. Represent the City at relevant library meetings as time
  and budget allows.

  b.  Develop and maintain an effective working relationship with the Board, which sets policy
  and oversees the budgetary expenditures on behalf of the Library including attending the
  monthly Board meeting, preparing staff reports and develop and engage Board members.

  c.  Develop and maintain an effective working relationship with City staff, elected officials
  and appointed officials and community groups such as the Friends of the Palmdale City
  Library. Be present at all City Council meetings as requested.

  conducting City Business.
  .  .

  ~re_ good drivers· and ensure thE;!Y are maintaining good driving habits.

  drives · while conducting City Business possesses a valid drivers license and a
  satisfactory driving record. Reviewing driving records will improve the overall driver
  quality and reduce the likelihood of accidents involving those who drive on City
  Business. Additionally, the City's insurance company recommends this practice to
  minimize potential liability.

  these laws and policies may result in the lo~s of driving privileges and/or disciplinary

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Construction Agreement No. A-8874 with Manhole Adjusting, Inc., for PN
  904, FY 2024-2025 Local Street ARAM Cape Seal Project for a not to exceed
  amount of $ 1,563,898, which includes a contract amount of $1,421,725 plus a
  10% contingency amount of $142,173; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8874
  with Manhole Adjusting, Inc., including minimal and/or non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

Project No. 904 will provide ARAM cape sealing on over 650,000 square feet of local
streets located at or near Avenue S & 47th Street East, Avenue S & 52nd Street East, and
Avenue S-8 & 45th Street East. ARAM cape seals are a sustainable pavement surface
treatment ideal for local streets in moderately distressed conditions. The installation
process generally includes resident notification, surface preparation (weed spraying and
crack sealing), localized repairs, a thin leveling course for the poorer-condition streets,
and a rubber-coated chip seal followed by a recycled-material slurry seal. Cul-de-sacs
and intersection stop points will receive a mill and asphalt-concrete overlay treatment to
provide greater strength for the heavy wheel turning and shear stresses associated with
these areas. The ARAM cape seal treatment is expected to extend the life of the existing
pavement surface by an additional 10 years.

BACKGROUND

In accordance with the Revenue and Tax Code (Sections 99 and 99.01), any time there
is a jurisdictional change, the County Auditor is required to adjust the allocation of
property tax revenue for local agencies whose services area or service responsibility
would be altered by the jurisdictional change. This adjustment or “Tax Sharing
Agreement” determines the distribution of the annual property tax among all affected
public agencies and special districts. The existing tax revenue based on the property’s
assessed value received by agencies will not change. This action only affects that
portion of future tax revenues based on increases in assessed property value.

DISCUSSION

The County Sanitation District No. 14 of Los Angeles County has requested that the City
enter into a tax-sharing agreement for parcel number 3204-025-048, as shown in
Attachment 1. The parcel is part of a proposed single-family residential housing
development (Tract No. 81337) located between 65th and 70th Streets West, south of
Avenue M. The project’s developer, DR Horton, has requested annexation into the
County Sanitation District No. 14. This annexation is a condition of the development’s
entitlement and is required before receiving sewer service.

The adoption of this Joint Tax Sharing Resolution will approve the City’s tax-sharing
agreement between public agencies currently receiving tax revenue from this parcel and
the County Sanitation District No. 14, which through the referenced annexation, will be
providing services to this parcel for the first time. All the referenced agencies and special
districts will execute and are party to the same Joint Tax Sharing Resolution. Staff
recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-071 and authorize the
Mayor to execute the Los Angeles County Joint Tax Sharing Resolution entitled
Annexation No. 454.

FISCAL IMPACT

The current property tax share ratio for the City of Palmdale within the area of this
annexation is 0.066294048 (6.6294%). This Council action will allocate 0.000396135
(0.0396%) of any future tax increase to the County Sanitation District No. 14. This results
in a net City tax share rate of 0.065897913 (6.5897%). For example, a tax increase
based on the assessed property value for this parcel will generate an additional $100 in
total property tax. The City would receive an additional $6.5897 of this increase, and the
County Sanitation District No. 14 would receive $0.0396. This allocation follows the
State Revenue and Taxation Code, and the allocation formula is established and
calculated by the Los Angeles County Auditor-Controller.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Consultant Agreement No. A-8881 with Psomas for PN 796, 45th Street
  East Trunk Sewer and Storm Drain Improvement Project, for a not to exceed
  amount of $338,514, which includes a contract amount of $307,740, plus a 10%
  contingency of $30,774, for a term of 42 weeks from the date of the Notice to
  Proceed; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8881
  with Psomas, including minimal and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND

In November 2019, the City Council awarded Design Agreement No. A-6797 for Project
No. 796, 45th Street East Trunk Sewer Project to Psomas which initiated the design of a
trunk sewer that would accommodate future commercial and residential development
south of Avenue S along 45th Street East. Once constructed, the sewer will be turned over
to the Los Angeles County Sanitation District for operation and maintenance pursuant to
Takeover Agreement No. A-6911. In prior years, Psomas worked on the design for this
project. However, the project was placed on hold pending assessment to accommodate
pending development.

The Trunk Sewer Extension design proved challenging because it accommodated the
connection of the smaller sewer lines currently serving the area and adjacent homes.
During the design, staff identified a missing element of the City’s Drainage Master Plan,
 Report to Mayor and City Council

which closely followed the Trunk Sewer alignment in 45th Street East. Further
investigation of the surface drainage in this area identified a significant benefit to
completing this missing link. Other benefits of combining the sewer and storm drain
designs avoid any utility conflicts and provide a more economical construction cost.

DISCUSSION

Agreement No. A-8881 will authorize Psomas to design the storm drain in 45th Street East
from Avenue R to Avenue R-8, coordinating the horizontal and vertical alignment with the
trunk sewer. Contracting with Psomas has several benefits for the City compared to
seeking another consultant. The majority of the preliminary work of researching utilities
and surveys has already been completed by Psomas. The consultant has determined
some changes to the original sewer design are needed to prevent any conflict between
these infrastructures. Finally, the horizontal and vertical alignment of the two projects is
so closely tied that having two different consultants would increase the possibility of
incompatibility of the final designs. As per Palmdale Municipal Code section 3.08.140
selecting Psomas based on their previous work is in the City’s best interest.

Psomas proposes to provide engineering design and project management services for
$307,740 for a term of 42 weeks.

PN 796 - 45th Street Storm Drain and Sewer Upgrades Project: (Exhbit A & B)

The City of Palmdale’s Master Plan of Drainage has defined a regional storm drain
main line within 45th Street East, which begins at the California aqueduct and runs
northerly to Avenue Q. Much of the regional mainline has previously been
constructed and functions as an existing storm drain system within the city’s overall
regional
plan. As part of the regional system within 45th Street East, the city has an existing
sixty-six (66") inch regional storm drain mainline between Avenue S and Avenue R-8,
that terminates at the southwest corner of the Avenue R-8 intersection. The existing
sixty-six (66") inch storm drain main line drops into a drywell chamber and flows from
larger storm events discharging to 45th Street East through a series of catch basins
constructed at the intersection. Reports from the city’s Maintenance Division indicate
that during recent storm events, stormwater ponding at the intersection has occurred,
and maintenance crews are cleaning the drainage ditch that runs along the shoulder
on the west side of 45th Street East.

To alleviate the current drainage condition, the city has requested to extend the
regional storm drain system, per the city’s Master Plan of Drainage, from Avenue R-8
to Avenue R, along 45th Street East. The storm drain extension will complete the

 connection of the existing system to the storm drain line located at the
intersection of Avenue R.

has expired.

Task 2.1 Topographic Survey
Psomas shall execute a Design Survey from the westerly right of way of 45th Street

East and north of Avenue R-8 from a client-supplied title report. Horizontal location,
size and description of, driveways, walks, curbs, walls, fences, signs, poles, trees
over six (6) inches in diameter, and other permanent surface visible features.
Horizontal and vertical location of approximately fifteen (15) potholes. Utilities from

Psomas’ potholing sub-consultant, Discovery Hydrovac, will conduct a maximum of

Discovery Hydrovac.

Task 2.4 30% Plans and Estimate
Psomas will prepare 30% design plans at a scale of 1”=40’ and cost estimate for the
project as follows:
• Storm Drain Plan: Psomas will prepare a Storm Drain Plan depicting preliminary
horizontal alignment and preliminary profiles of the proposed storm drain system. All
comments received during the Alignment and Elevation Concept Workshop will be
incorporated into this submittal. Pipeline stationing, catch basin locations, annotation,
and construction notes will be minimally shown at this submittal stage.
• Street Improvement Plan: Psomas will prepare Street Improvement Plans that show
pavement widening improvements at a scale of 1” = 40’ on the west side of 45th
Street between Wrightwood Way and Avenue R-8, a distance of approximately 1,900
feet, up to an ultimate gutter line. The ultimate gutter line is understood to be the

sewer mainlines within 45th Street East, from Avenue R to Avenue S

future development flows. This project shall replace existing public sewer
mainlines, where pipe sizes range from ten (10) inch to fifteen (15) inch VCP,

+Sttr Street East. LASCD has determined eligibility of accepting ownership and
maintenance of said eighteen (18) inch relief, once constructed.

  FOR A COMBINED TOTAL OF $203,500 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-
  2025

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Award Invitation for Bid No. 24-003-3610 with SiteOne Landscape Supply and
  Wilbur-Ellis Company for fertilizer supplies each for an amount not to exceed
  $101,750, for a combined total of $203,500 for Fiscal Year 2024-2025;

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to approve Requisition No. 250083
  and resulting Purchase Orders with SiteOne Landscape Supply, including minimal
  and/or non-substantial changes; and,

  3. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to approve Requisition No. 250084
  and resulting Purchase Orders with Wilbur-Ellis, including minimal and/or non-
  substantial changes.

  4. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to exercise the option to extend each
  resulting Purchase Order for two additional one-year terms, including minimal
  and/or non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

The Maintenance Division uses fertilizer supplies to maintain the health of landscape
plants and turf in City Parks, Landscape Maintenance Districts, General Benefits,
Palmdale Transportation Center, Park and Rides, and Fairway Business Park. These
supplies are essential for sustainable best management practices of grounds and green
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Requisition Nos. 250083 & 250084

Page 2

spaces, maintaining landscape quality, and providing safe and attractive public spaces
and infrastructure.

DISCUSSION

The City released Invitation for Bid (IFB) No. 24-004-3610 for fertilizer supplies on April
8, 2024. Notification of the IFB release was sent electronically to registered vendors on
PlanetBids. The solicitation was also published in the Antelope Valley Press.

Four (4) bids were received on May 15, 2024, and are summarized below:

  Bidder  Location  Unit Price Total
  SiteOne Landscape Supply  Palmdale, CA  $418.54
  Wilbur-Ellis Company  Ontario, CA  $520.79
  Target Specialty Products  Santa Fe Springs, CA  $705.15
  Nutrien Ag Solutions  Perris, CA  $804.49

The Notice of Intent to Award was issued to SiteOne Landscape Supply and Wilbur-Ellis
Company on May 29, 2024. Staff elected to multi-award because each vendor offered the
lowest pricing on specific materials used. Additionally, having two vendors, including a
local company, will improve the City’s access and ability to procure these materials when
needed.

The resulting Purchase Orders will each have a one year term for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.
The City reserves the right and option to extend the term of each Purchase Order for two
additional one-year periods upon mutual consent of the same terms and conditions with
the vendor.

FISCAL IMPACT

$203,500; Funds for the Requisitions (each $101,750) and resulting blanket Purchase
Orders will be budgeted in supply accounts: Park Maintenance (10133002-737107),
Palmdale Transportation Center (20333005-737107-3410), Park and Rides (20333005-
735100-3411), Landscape Maintenance Districts (25133003-737107-3610), General
Benefit Landscapes (10133003-737107), and Fairway Business Park (10133003-
737107-1087).

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Award Invitation for Bid No. 24-004-3610 with SiteOne Landscape Supply for
  irrigation and water conservation supplies in an amount not to exceed $284,000
  for Fiscal Year 2024-2025; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to approve Requisition No. 250082
  and the resulting Purchase Order with SiteOne Landscape Supply for an amount
  not to exceed $284,000, including minimal and/or non-substantial changes.

  3. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to exercise the option to extend the
  resulting Purchase Order for two additional one-year terms, including minimal
  and/or non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

The Maintenance Division manages irrigation system infrastructure and landscapes in
City Parks, Palmdale Transportation Center, Park and Rides, Landscape Maintenance
Districts, General Benefit Landscape Areas, and Fairway Business Park. Supplies, such
as nozzles, bubblers, valves, couplings, PVC piping, controllers, diaphragms, backflows,
enclosures, and other related items, are essential for maintaining sustainable best
management practices of grounds and green spaces to ensure landscape quality and
water conservation efforts for the community.

DISCUSSION

The City released Invitation for Bid (IFB) No. 24-004-3610 for irrigation and water
conservation supplies on April 10, 2024. Notification of the IFB release was sent
electronically to registered vendors on PlanetBids. The solicitation was also published in
the Antelope Valley Press.

Two (2) bids were received on May 16, 2024, and are summarized below:

  Bidder  Location  Unit Price Total
  SiteOne Landscape Supply  Palmdale, CA  $18,095.94
  Smith Pipe & Supply, Inc.  Lancaster, CA  $21,612.52

The Notice of Intent to Award was issued to SiteOne Landscape Supply on May 29,
2024.

The resulting Purchase Order will be for one year for Fiscal Year 2024-2025. The City
reserves the right and option to extend the term for two additional one-year periods upon
mutual consent of the same terms and conditions with the vendor.

$284,000; Funds for the requisition and resulting blanket Purchase Order is budgeted in

3411), Landscape Maintenance Districts (25133003-734110-3610), General Benefit
Landscapes (10133003-734110), and Fairway Business Park (10133003-734110-1087).

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-073, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
  Palmdale declaring its intention to conduct a public hearing to consider the
  vacation of portions of 8th Street East south of Rancho Vista Boulevard and north
  of Avenue P-8;

  2. Authorize the Mayor to execute Resolution No. CC 2024-073 declaring the
  intention to conduct a public hearing to consider the vacation of portions of 8th
  Street East south of Rancho Vista Boulevard and north of East Avenue P-8; and,

  3. Set the time and place for a public hearing on October 2, 2024, to consider the
  proposed vacation.

BACKGROUND

In conjunction with developing their commercial building, Covington Development
Partners, LLC, applied for street vacation in March 2024. The developer is requesting
the vacation of portions of the existing right of way along the frontage of their
development located on the west side of 8th Street East south of Rancho Vista Boulevard
and north of East Avenue P-8 (AIN 3022-001-027). The street vacation has been
requested in conjunction with the approval of the project improvement plans and as a
condition of approval for Site Plan Review (SPR22-012). Following the review and
adoption of this development by the Planning Commission (PC-2023-017), it was
 Report to Mayor and City Council

determined that any potential adverse environmental impacts could be mitigated and
would, therefore, be insignificant.

DISCUSSION

The property that makes up this current commercial building project was previously part
of an auto storage development. As such, it was conditioned to dedicate additional right-
of-way to specifically serve their land use. The right-of-way dedication included multiple
driveway locations and a right-turn pocket. Unfortunately, the auto storage developer
never completed their project and no new public improvements were ever constructed.

The off-site improvements for the current commercial building development (SPR 22-
012) were evaluated during the entitlement process and it was determined that the
previously conditioned right turn lane, one driveway, and several expanded entry curb
radii along 8th Street East were no longer necessary. Therefore, the previously dedicated
right-of-way is the subject of this proposed street vacation.

Pursuant to the Streets and Highway Code, Section 8320, the local agency (City)
processing the street vacation under the General Vacation Procedure shall initiate the
vacation proceedings by setting the date, hour, and place for a public hearing. This
action will be followed by notification to public utility providers, posting notices at the
property, and publication of the vacation information and public hearing schedule within
the local newspaper.

FISCAL IMPACT

$0; There is no fiscal impact to the City as a result of this action.

  1) Nominate and appoint one (1) member to the Library Board of Trustees for the
  remainder of a term to expire on June 30, 2026; and,

  2) Nominate and appoint one (1) alternate member to the Library Board of Trustees
  to fill any unscheduled vacancy created by one of the sitting members.

BACKGROUND

The City’s Library Board appointments are made in accordance with Section 2.32.020 of
the Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC). Trustees are appointed by the Mayor with the
majority approval of the City Council. In June 2024, the Council adopted Ordinance No.
1642, establishing an alternate member position. Appointing an alternate to fill any vacant
position that may arise helps to ensure the continuity of the Library Board. Trustees serve
a three-year term and must reside in the City of Palmdale.

DISCUSSION

There are currently two vacant seats on the board. An unscheduled vacancy was
created due to the resignation of Library Board Trustee Orellano, with a term expiring
on June 30, 2026. The adoption of Ordinance No. 1642, establishing an alternate trustee
